About the Workshop

Stochastic Parrots or World-Modellers?

What does it mean for a system trained exclusively on text to genuinely represent and understand the world?

Since the public release of ChatGPT in late 2022, large language models (LLMs) have become a fixture of academic and public life. Yet how these systems operate, and what they are fundamentally capable of, remains poorly understood by many of its users. While many are aware that such systems are trained to predict the most likely next word (or rather token) given a context, far fewer have reflected on capacities emerging from this simple training objective, and the further implications of fine-tuning via reinforcement learning through human feedback and verifiable rewards.

An interesting starting point for the debate is a thought experiment proposed by Bender and Koller (2020) involving an infinitely smart octopus intercepting underwater telegraphic communications between two islanders. Can the octopus genuinely output meaningful text about the land-world after eavesdropping on vast amounts of the islanders’ communication about what happens there, without ever engaging with that world directly? This analogy is meant to raise the following sharper question: can an LLM’s internal states and outputs be about extra-linguistic reality, independently of the meaning human interpreters project onto them?

This workshop gathers philosophers and AI researchers to address this question and other related issues.

Online registration, first-come first-served. Primarily for the Geneva and Neuchâtel communities in philosophy, linguistics, and computer science. Students warmly welcome.

Programme

Talks and discussion
The two-day workshop combines speaker sessions, shared discussion, and unconference time.

How to get there

  • From Geneva Cornavin train station: take tram 15 or 17 to Cirque, then walk about 5 minutes to Rue des Savoises 15.
  • From Geneva Airport: take the train to Geneva Cornavin, then tram 15 or 17 to Cirque. The airport-to-Cornavin train takes about 7 minutes.
  • Nearby stops: Cirque is served by tram 15, tram 17, bus 1, bus 2, and bus 19; Place de Neuve is also within walking distance.

Sign up for the event

Attendance is limited to 30 non-speaker participants (workshop) on a first-come, first-served basis. To register your interest, send us an email under subject heading: Bookworm with a short note on your affiliation (if applicable), background and motivation until 31 October — we will confirm your place and keep you informed of all updates, the final schedule, and reading materials ahead of the event then. Student participants are very welcome!
